claim: The kernel uses small quantized activation-dependent tables and AVX2/NEON register lookups over low-bit weight planes. Intel testing includes an i5-1035G7, not the local Ryzen 3600X. Its published speedups are not measurements of this project or this donor.
The maintainers explicitly do not guarantee significant speedups, especially for 4-bit generation, on all older x86 systems. Windows support has additional toolchain requirements.

Small additive codebooks enable CPU lookup kernels, but CPU layer speedups use an eight-core Intel i9 FP32 baseline. Default 7B quantization is about one A100 day, and default full-model tuning adds 3–6 hours on four A100s. This does not establish a cheap local 3060 conversion.

Quantization sensitivity differs across recurrent input, state groups and output projection. Channel/head reordering must preserve the recurrence and match convolution, norm and output projection. Output-space Hadamard plus GPTQ improves the paper's W4A16 result relative to simple group quantization. The GPU results do not establish CPU speed or Falcon native-96 equivalence.
